extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners before the USPTO (patent attorneys and agents); parties involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, obligations, and sanctions governing the professional conduct of patent practitioners before the USPTO, including duties on limited-scope representation, communication, diligence, withdrawal, probation reporting, remedial measures, and consequences for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.102(c) — informed consent for limited-scope representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule § 11.102(c) requires obtaining a client's informed consent for limited-scope (unbundled) representation and appropriate steps when the limited scope ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the respondent violated § 11.102(c) by "failing to obtain his client's informed consent to limited-scope representation on a 'project' basis in the application and failing to withdraw from representation after the limited scope representation was complete." When offering limited-scope services, a practitioner must obtain informed consent detailing the scope and must withdraw when that scope is complete (and notify client/USPTO as appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(1)-(3) — client communication and consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule § 11.104(a)(1)-(3): promptly inform the client of any decision or circumstance requiring the client's informed consent; reasonably consult with the client about the means to accomplish objectives; keep the client reasonably informed about the status of a matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites failures including "failing to timely provide the client with the final Office Action, failing to respond to the final Office Action without the client's consent, allowing the application to become abandoned without the client's consent, and failing to timely provide the client with the Notice of Abandonment." These specific examples illustrate what constitutes a breach of the communication and consultation duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 — reasonable diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule § 11.103 requires a practitioner to act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The respondent admitted violation by "failing to timely notify the client of the final Office Action, failing to respond to the Office Action, allowing the application to become abandoned without the client's consent, failing to notify the client of the Notice of Abandonment in the application, and failing to take steps to revive the abandoned application." These conduct examples are provided as concrete failures of diligence and promptness.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.116(a)(3) — withdrawal when practitioner is discharged
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule § 11.116(a)(3) requires a practitioner to withdraw from representation when discharged by the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order found a violation where the respondent "failed to notify the client and the USPTO of his withdrawal from representation after the limited-scope representation of each 'project' in the client's application was complete." Practitioners must effectuate withdrawal and notify both client and USPTO when representation terminates.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.116(d) — duties upon termination to protect client's interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule § 11.116(d) obligates a practitioner upon termination of representation to take steps reasonably practicable to protect a client's interests (e.g., give reasonable notice, allow time to hire other counsel, surrender papers/property, refund unearned fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states the respondent violated § 11.116(d) by "failing to notify the client and the USPTO of his withdrawal ... and failing to timely provide the client with a copy of the final Office Action and Notice of Abandonment." Examples of protective steps include notice, time for successor counsel, surrendering client property, and refunding unearned fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when providing limited-scope ('unbundled') representation
rubrics_metrics.description: When representing a client on a limited-scope or 'project' basis, the practitioner must obtain informed consent regarding the limited scope and must comply with withdrawal and termination duties under the Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly states: "if he enters into a client relationship based on limited scope representation by project ... he must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.102(c) and must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.116." Practically, this means clear informed-consent documentation, timely withdrawal/notification at project completion, and steps to protect the client's interests at termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to timely notify clients of Office communications and Notices of Abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must promptly report Office communications (e.g., Office Actions, Notices of Abandonment) to clients and counsel them in time to take appropriate action; they must take steps to revive abandoned applications where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists concrete failures: respondent "received a final Office Action ... and failed to report the Office Action to the client until [~18 months later]," "failed to respond to the Office Action prior to the due date, resulting in the application being abandoned," "failed to report the Notice of Abandonment to the client," and "did not take any action to revive the abandoned application." These are examples of conduct inconsistent with communication and diligence rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation reporting requirements (24-month probation — reports every 12 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: During the 24-month probation, respondent must submit reports to OED Director at 12 and 24 months containing specified information about U.S. utility patent applications that received a Notice of Abandonment predicated on failure to timely and/or properly respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required report contents (numbered as in the Final Order): (1) identify by application number each affected U.S. utility patent application; (2) state whether, how and when respondent reported the Office communication to the client prior to abandonment; (3) provide documentary evidence that respondent reported the Office communication to the client (e.g., correspondence copies); (4) state whether, how and when respondent reported the Notice of Abandonment to the client; (5) state whether, how and when respondent counseled the client about the abandonment, including whether counseling occurred in adequate time to avoid abandonment; (6) provide documentary evidence that respondent reported the Notice of Abandonment and counseled the client (e.g., correspondence copies); (7) for each application where respondent did not counsel the client in adequate time, identify application number and client name/address and provide detailed explanation why respondent failed to counsel in time; and (8) if no applications fall under (1)-(7), affirmatively report that there are no such applications to report. These items create measurable documentary and substantive reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and procedural steps for probation noncompliance — Order to Show Cause and suspension request
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED Director believes the respondent failed to comply with the Agreement, Final Order, or Rules, OED may issue an Order to Show Cause and, after procedures, request the USPTO Director to suspend the respondent for up to twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural steps set forth: (e)(1) OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause and send it to respondent's last address of record; respondent has 15 days to respond; (e)(2) if OED Director remains of the opinion noncompliance occurred, OED shall deliver to the USPTO Director the Order to Show Cause, respondent's response (if any), and OED's argument/evidence, and request that the USPTO Director enter an order suspending respondent up to 12 months for the violations listed in the Joint Legal Conclusions. The Order also preserves OED's ability to seek discrete discipline for misconduct forming the basis of the Order to Show Cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial practice-management measures the Office considered as mitigating
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner's remedial measures (accepted by OED as mitigating factors) include implementing a computer-based docketing system, contracting a document retention system, hiring a secretarial/paralegal person, holding/restoring funds to reimburse petition-to-revive fees, and providing full disclosures to OED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists the docketing system features: (a) automatically dockets statutory due dates (including extensions) upon entry of the mailing date of an action; (b) sends email reminders; and (c) for trademark applications, automatically dockets filings and monitors status changes by communicating with USPTO online systems. The practitioner also contracted to implement a document retention system and hired support staff. The Order notes the respondent is willing to reimburse the former client's petition-to-revive fee and will hold that money in escrow pending determination. These measures are cited as factors considered in mitigation of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Legal Education (CLE) requirement — case management training
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must, within six months of the Final Order, enroll, complete and receive CLE credit under the Michigan State Bar for at least one course whose primary subject is case management (e.g., calendaring and communicating with clients) for small firms/solo practitioners, and within seven months provide corroborating proof of completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof required includes: (a) documentary evidence of attendance and completion of the case management course; (b) a description of the course content for which credit was received; and (c) a copy of all written materials provided to course participants or other corroborating proof acceptable to the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and future-consideration of disciplinary record
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order and the disciplinary record will be electronically published in OED's Reading Room and a notice will be published in the Official Gazette; the record will be considered in future complaints or disciplinary proceedings and may be used as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs electronic publication at the OED Reading Room and publication of a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided Notice of Public Reprimand and Probation text. The Order states the record may be considered: (1) when addressing further complaints or similar conduct; and/or (2) in future disciplinary proceedings as an aggravating factor and/or to rebut statements made on respondent's behalf.
